record_notes.DCP-LETT-1679: May 8 with supplied 1855 year. Gives earlier published boulder reference, calls proportional ice-dressing argument new, and discusses viscosity/momentum manuscript appended to Ramsay paper. Wants to recover manuscript and perhaps publish it; August publication is future. Hopkins support recalled from earlier meeting, and Geological Society criticism refers to Lyell telling him, not necessarily a surviving letter. Does not answer April 23 Barrande/Dana source 1672; topics and identified inputs differ. Missing glacial enquiry and oral exchanges cannot be replaced by nearby catalogue record.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1772: November 4 with supplied 1855 year. Returns two Bachman pamphlets with evaluative criticism showing some reading, but exact pamphlet identities remain probable in summary. This does not imply reading Nott/Gliddon book, which apparatus dates to December. Pigeon pairs already alive, external observation underway, skeletonising planned; plant varieties and hybrids begun. Invitation remains prospective. P6 says he has just seen Lubbock and learned that New Zealand Flora was sent with Wollaston work; no blanket inference of Lyell receipt or reading. Later November 28 scientific journal remains future. No surviving incoming pamphlet cover or Lyell prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1630: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. January 14 with supplied 1855 year. House-hunting January 12–13 delayed response; hopes house secured but is not sure, contrary to editorial summary saying found. Grampian source remembered as read or heard from Sharpe, with apparatus identifying a geographic mismatch; no forced certainty. Distinguishes association from overlying and demands dip as well as strike evidence. Verified raw MathML is four and one-half feet, not 412 feet. Full enclosed sketch viewed: shallow strata/quartz layers crossed by steeper foliation, with labels and quartz folia. It depicts proposed molecular redistribution, not proof of all geology. Some gneiss may be fluid; not all. Missing Lyell objection is not supplied by Darwin January 10 letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1633: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. Sunday within January 21–February 11, 1855 XML range; calendar candidates are January 21/28 or February 4/11, without one established day. Lyell letter forwarded from Down and now received; exact arrival unknown. Concedes serious gap: parallel foliation/cleavage was assumed distinct from bedding where that cannot be proved. Recalled earlier curve idea and tuff crystallisation case remain author claims. Actual P4 diagram shows quartz nodules and feldspar crystals in parallel layers, with no quantitative scale. Sorby paper not yet obtained. Conditional P.S. distinguishes metamorphosed clay-slate cleavage from other rocks stratification, not a settled universal resolution. Later published consensus not activated here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1672: Explicit prior primary full reading reused with matching pins. April 23, 1855 incoming Lyell letter advocates Barrande foreign membership and endorses Dana. Distinguishes published merit from unpublished discoveries Lyell personally saw; thirty gastropod genera/150 species and 150 bivalves are Lyell reported evidence, with claim about Forbes polarity qualified nearly overturned. Proposed Cambrian terminology and French support are current opinion, not later uncontested history. No preceding Darwin letter survives to pair this reverse response. No automatic receipt on composition/council day. Independently located June 10 Darwin-to-Huxley 1697 explicitly encloses this old Lyell note in the same Barrande/Dana campaign, establishing a conservative known-by witness then. Later election failure and Dana 1884 election remain future.
